title: Chapter 12
text: ∫ portrait of a soul for flies he is a man in a thinning undershirt of faded revolution advancing the mathematics of his impurity to the final zero and awakening this morning with the taste of salmon on my tongue I thought of him although I felt like I needed a priest or at least his housewoman to stroke my private parts back to some speck of majesty there is a letter in his hand from a rich man in Santa Fe: “you’re slipping, you’re slipping, V. and I who have been fans of yours for years are seriously worried about your artistic decline—even tho your popularity still seems to be climbing. why don’t you see a psychiatrist and get the cork blown out of your ass? J.” the Alka-Seltzer tablets spider-crawl to life as his white cat sits inside the window looking at him my cat looks good, he thinks, my cat doesn’t have to keep MAKING IT in the all-American grind and he puts his nose his all-American nose into the sharp bubbles the cat never needs and drinks the bubbles while sweat of last night’s 18 beers and pint of scotch moil down his ears and neck I should call Fat Freddy the Turdhurler I should find a brass mountain to hide my costermonger’s psyche under a bird rises in the brush outside caught between the sun and himself and the shade of a huge wing-shadow passes over him passes over the house-edge— the cat leaps against the screen and everything is older than Normandy and Stalingrad and the shelling of the harbors Winston Churchill with child’s brain spittle on his chin waves to the love-fogged crowd from the tall window and then he’s dead like almost everything else but the man in the thinning undershirt: his cat is angry the screen has cheated him and the cat’s yellow eyes come down to his like the eyes of a small businessman who once fired him for loafing in the stockroom “shit on you,” he tells the cat, “and shit on all the untalented demeanors of my dwindling talent.” 30 minutes later that first bottle of beer is better than any sex anywhere in the world with any big-assed cow that he ever ripped the silk and lace from he goes into the bedroom where his woman sits rocking his child in her belly and he takes the cigarette out of her hand puts it to his mouth and coughs coughs coughs and still the dwindling talent he thinks, I’ve heard that cough before: a horse chunking wash of saliva past iron bit while pulling his first junkwagon through a frosty useless morning in some small city where only one man owns a Mercedes he is sweating he must stink but the walls are polite and he holds one half a beer in a bottle and the woman says, “I hope you didn’t mean all those things you said last night.” “ah, just the good things.” “well, that narrows it down. you’re not going to drink today?” “just a little, sweetie. I’m a coward.” “feed the cat.” “yeah.” at the door is a Western Union boy. he gives him an unsubstantial tip and the boy runs off sweating the American hustler God save him THE DEADLINE FOR OUR ORIGINAL POETRY ISSUE OUT IN SEPTEMBER IS AUGUST 17TH WOULD APPRECIATE YOUR CONTRIBUTING TO THIS UNIQUE ISSUE BEST WISHES GENE COLE INTERMISSION MAGAZINE 3212 NORTH BROADWAY CHICAGO ILL “did somebody die?” he hands her the telegram “ooo, you’re famous!” “I can see it now: me and Genet and Sartre sharing a drink at a sidewalk cafe in Paree.” “who are they?” “nobody. other genii.” “oh. well, feed the cat.” so I fed the cat drank 18 more cans of beer and wrote this.
